title: Clavicular Admits Girlfriend Shaving Head to Prevent Giving Him Acne Was ‘Amazing Bait’
text:

Join MyComplex Unlock rewards SHOP STYLE SNEAKERS MUSIC SPORTS POP CULTURE BETS COVER STORIES VERZUZ WATCH COMMUNITY Pop Culture Clavicular Admits Girlfriend Shaving Head to Prevent Giving Him Acne Was ‘Amazing Bait’
 The looksmaxxing streamer's video of his girlfriend buzzing off her hair drew heavy criticism. 
 By Jade Gomez November 16, 2026 Comments Comment Save Share Comments Comments Key Takeaways
 Clavicular posted a video of girlfriend Lily Snyder shaving her head, initially claiming she did it to prevent hair-product residue from giving him acne before calling that explanation “bait.” 
 Snyder defended the haircut with “My body, my choice,” while Clavicular later claimed she intended to donate her hair to a family member with cancer and said she asked him to remove the video. 
 The looksmaxxing streamer, whose real name is Braden Peters, also faces a Nov. 24 probable cause hearing after pleading not guilty to charges that he raped a 17-year-old; he denies the allegation. 
 Controversial “looksmaxxing” streamer Clavicular is facing a wave of criticism after he posted a video of his girlfriend, Lily Snyder, shaving her head so her hair wouldn't give him acne.
 On Sunday night (Nov. 15), the streamer shared a clip on X in which Snyder sits in front of a mirror and runs clippers through her long blonde hair while he films. 
 "Nocturnal facial contact with a woman's hair may expose skin to comedogenic hair-product residue, causing acne,” the caption said. “My girlfriend in an attempt to aid me in my looksmaxxing journey shaved all of her hair off. Very loving gesture, bare minimum IOI."
 His reps told TMZ that Snyder is "perfectly happy" with the new look, has "zero regrets," and keeps comparing herself to singer Sinéad O'Connor, who was known for keeping a close-cropped haircut. They added that the couple "frequently discusses how hair products can contribute to breakouts."
 Clavicular appeared to be the one who proposed the shave, pitching it as a way to raise awareness about acne, but his rep maintains Snyder would never have gone along with it against her wishes. His rep also claims she had already wanted to donate her long hair, and although bleached hair may not qualify, she bagged it and "still plans to explore donation options."
 Snyder addressed the shave on X herself, writing "Donating my hair to a loved one" over a photo of a zip-lock bag stuffed with her hair. She also hit back at critics:
 "Stop saying I'm unwell because I chose to be stylish and hot and shave my head like Sinead O'Connor and Britney Spears. My body, my choice."
 Clavicular then gave a different explanation in follow-up posts and alleged the acne reasoning was fake, writing, "This is a shit post. She's donating her hair to a family member who has cancer. I just knew this would be an amazing bait lol."
 He also said Snyder had asked him to take the original video down. He admitted he was torn because it might be the "best bait in Twitter history," but decided removing it was the smarter move since looksmaxxing already carries a "bad reputation."
 Clavicular, real name is Braden Peters, built his following online pushing “looksmaxxing,” or the practice of enhancing one’s attractiveness, which includes extreme measures such as bonesmashing, a pseudoscientific practice of striking facial bones with a hammer or fist to “shape” one’s bone structure. He has also admitted to using meth to suppress his appetite .
 His relationship with Snyder has been on and off since they met on stream in April. They broke up during a Kick stream in July , got back together, split again in mid-September, and were dating again as of October.
 Peters is also in legal hot water, having recently pleaded not guilty Oct. 22 in Orleans, Mass. to charges that he raped a 17-year-old at his family's Chatham home in May 2025. Through his lawyers, he denies the allegation and says the encounter was consensual.
 He is due back in court Tuesday, Nov. 24, for a probable cause hearing, where a judge will decide whether the case goes forward.
